reasons.A: Short, repetitive, plain sentences and a chatty second-person 'you' stance are far from the passage's convoluted, Latinate, parenthesis-laden syntax and formal detachment.
reasons.B: Measured, formal, third-person treatment of the clerk echoes the passage's detached stance, but its sentences run smooth and modern, without the author's inversions, stacked clauses or odd compression.
reasons.C: Closest in movement and diction: long, stacked clauses, a Latinate period register ('attached some importance', 'disposed of'), semicolons and a generalising view of the shop assistant's position, though it uses 'I' where the author uses 'we' and slips in one contraction.
